text:
Day trading isn't a video game—here’s the brutal reality: 🛑

The $25K Rule & Trade Limit: If you execute 4 or more day trades in 5 days, you trigger Pattern Day Trader rules requiring a $25,000 minimum in a margin account.

Borrowed Money: Margin gives you leverage, meaning you're trading with borrowed broker funds to amplify your bets.

You Can Lose MORE Than You Put In: Unlike standard investing where you only lose your stake, margin trading can leave you actually owing your broker real money if a trade tanks.

Know the risks before playing with fire. 🔥📉

Now, I am not completely against using some new cool tech to try and make some money in the financial markets but, far safer option is through something like Kalshi probability market.

Also, if you want to do some swing trading and have an AI agent help pick those investment options that might move say 5 or 10 percent over the next few days or week; much safer because it should not require a margin account.

This not investment advice, always do your own research or consult a licensed professional  ... have fun but, don't risk what you can't afford to lose!

text:
I think that the workflow you got going on is too slow for day trading. I think you may have more success if your agents are geared towards longer positions, from a few days up to a month. I think that on that time scale trends become a little more predictable, and there is less urgency to trade the news the moment they come out. 

Trading the daily news requires high speed. Serious high frequency day traders are working on shaving off milliseconds from their workflows. By the time your agents listen to the news, leave each other notes, send and read e-mails, the news is already priced-in when you finally execute a trade.

text:
It’s way more complicated than Ready, Set, Trade. 
Even if you imagine GPT can articulate a strategy, it’s still on you to set what developers would call a workspace. You should define:
1. Expectation
2. Risk tolerance 
3. Time horizon. 
Then you were to define the strategy tools (quant, technical, fundamental, news, insider trading). 
You did nothing but effectively throw darts at a board. 
The conventional mantra of amateurs, “I should've, I could've,” is the best recipe for a disaster. 
Beating the S&P 500 on a short window is nonsense, as the markets overall are random noise the shorter the period. 
Markets are Markov processes by nature. 
All your technical videos are amazing. I love them. This video is … oh well!… You can take it down to minimize the damage.
And the thumbnail is deceiving for the first time.

text:
Viewers should be careful about treating this video as evidence that AI can trade profitably. By the creator’s own figures, the account finished at $9,900 versus $9,980 for the S&P 500: a 1% loss and 0.8 percentage points of underperformance.
Throughout the challenge, he repeatedly pushes the system to trade more, removes filters, and increases exposure because he is frustrated with inactivity. Saying he would rather lose $500 than see little activity is a major red flag. More trades and less cash do not mean better decisions.
With frequent human interventions, changing rules, and only seven trading days, this experiment cannot establish a reliable trading edge. Screenshots alone also do not independently verify that this was real money.
The pressure to produce an exciting video is driving the experiment. Don’t confuse that with a validated investment strategy.
